slides.texte_overlay:
weird psychology tricks
that actually work

the gentle nod

nod slightly while you ask someone for something. people mirror small movements without noticing, so a soft nod makes saying yes feel more natural to them.

the warm cup

offer a warm drink before a difficult chat. research suggests warmth in the hands makes people see others as warmer, kinder and easier to trust overall.

the three second pause

when someone gives a short answer, stay quiet for three seconds. most people fill the silence with the real answer, the one they were quietly holding back.

the curious effect

people listen more closely to someone who knows a little about everything, and you can build that in minutes a day. a few curious minutes daily quietly change how people respond to you.

the name at goodbye

say someone's name at the end of a goodbye rather than at the start of a hello. it's the last thing they hear from you, and it stays with them longer.
